      Engine No. 1's Comments ill Respome to PUCT Staff's ReeomlHIHlatiell Memo


                                         I.   Introduction
     Engine No. 1 submits these comments in response to the April 12, 2026 Memorandum issued
by Public Utility Commission of Texas ("Commission'') Staff recommending criteria for
Commission guidance on ERCOT' s Batch Zero interconnection process ("Staff Memo"). Engine
No. 1 appreciates Commission Staff's thoughtful engagement with this complex and consequential
proceeding and offers the following comments to supplement, clarify, and expand upon the
reoommendations set forth in the Staff Memo.
      Engine No. 1 is an investment firm that builds and invests in companies powering innovation
and reindustrialization in the United States, with significant interests in large load development in
the ERCOT region. Engine No. 1 has actively participated in ERCOT's PGRR 145 stakeholder
process and has submitted comments regarding Batch Zero eligibility criteria, including criteria
applicable to Bring Your Own Generation ("BYOG'') co-location projects. Engine No. 1
respectfully urges the Commission to consider the BYOG issues a d ~ below in providing
guidance to ERCOT and stakeholders as they work toward finalizing PGRR 145.

 IL    COIIUllission Staff's Memoraadum Does Not Address BYOG Eligibility Criteri.--A
                                    Gap That Must Be Filled
      Engine No. 1 respectfully calls the Commission's attention to a significant omission in the
Staff Memo: it does not address Bring Your Own Generation ("BYOG") co-location projects or
propose any criteria governing their eligibility for inclusion in Batch Zero. This gap, if left
unaddresse<L threatens to exclude an entire category of viable, reliability-positive projects from
Batch Zer~ntrary to ERCOT's own expressed interest in facilitating BYOG participation and
contrary to the Commission's obligation to ensure that the Batch Zero process operates fairly and
prediot.ably for all large load interconnection models.
      BYOG projects pair new generation resources-typically wind, solar, and/or gas-with a
co-located large load behind a shared point of interconnection ("POI'.,). These projects may help
advance grid reliability by adding new generation capacity while serving incremental load, and
ERCOT bas indicated that BYOG co-location is a preferred model for meeting the scale of
interconnection demand currently in the queue. Critically, however, BYOG projects undergo
interconnection study through the generator's Full Interconnection Study ("FIS") process rather



                                                  1
 than a standalone Large Load Interconnection Study ("LLIS'')-meanin g that existing Batch Zero
eligibility criteria based solely on LLIS completion will structurally exclude BYOG projects,
regardless of their development maturity.
      The Commission should direct ERCOT and stakeholders to incorporate BYOG eligibility
criteria into the final PGRR 145. As a basis for that discussion, Engine No. 1 respectfully offers
for the Commission's consideration the four options detailed in Section ill below, which Engine
No. 1 submitted as proposed PGRR 145 language in the ongoing stakeholder process.

                     UL     Four Options for BYOG Batch Zero Eligibility
      Engine No. I acknowledges, with appreciation, the responsiveness and diligence that
ERCOT staff have demonstrated throughout the PGRR 145 stakeholder process in evaluating
eligibility criteria for large load customers that propose to bring their own generation. ERCOT' s
willingness to engage substantively on BYOG co-location structures throughout its Batch Zero
discussions spanning seven stakeholder workshops demonstrates their serious and good-faith
effort to develop a framework that accommodates innovative interconnection models while
preserving grid reliability. Engine No. 1 commends ERCOT for this work and submits the
following options in that same constructive spirit.
      The four options set forth below were filed with ERCOT on April 8, 2026, as part of Engine
No. l's comments on PGRR 145 in the ongoing ERCOT stakeholder process. Engine No. 1 is
including these options in this filing in the spirit of transparency, so that the Commission has full
visibility into the BYOG eligibility framework currently under consideration at ERCOT-and so
that the Commission may, in its discretion, provide guidance on this matter now or at such future
time as it deems appropriate.
      Engine No. 1 proposes four independent options for BYOG eligibility under PGRR 145, two
addressing Base Load qualification under Section 9.2.1.1 and two addressing Studied Load
qualification under Section 9.2.1.2. Each option is designed to be self-contained and to
accommodate different BYOG project structures, depending on whether the load and generation
are studied jointly under a single FIS or under separate FIS and ILLE applications sharing a
common POI.
Option 1 (Base Load - Single FIS Pathway): The Large Load has requested an Initial
Energization date on or after January 1, 2028, and ERCOT has determined that the Large Load
was included in a Full Interconnection Study (FIS) for a new large Generation Resource and
completed the requirements in Section 5.3.2.2, Full Interconnection Study Scoping Process, as a
co-located Large Load, by July I 0, 2026. The FIS must reflect the full requested Load amount and
conform to all study requirements detailed in Section 5.3.2.2.
Option 2 (Base Load - Dual FIS+ ILLE Pathway): The Large Load has requested an Initial
Energization date on or after January I, 2028, and ERCOT has determined that the Large Load
was included in an LLIS request submitted to ERCOT and completed the requirements in Section
9.3.2, Large Load Interconnection Study Scoping Process, by July 10, 2026; and ERCOT has


                                                  2
 detennined that the ILLE is co~located with a Generation Resource under a Full Interconnection
Study for a new large Generation Resource and completed the requirements in Section 5.3.2.2 by
July 10, 2026. The LLIS and the FIS must be co-located at a single POI, POIB, or Service Delivery
Point.
Option 3 (Studied Load - Single FIS Pathway): The Large Load has requested an Initial
Energization date on or after January 1, 2028, and ERCOT has determined that the Large Load
was included in a Full Interconnection Study (FIS) for a new large Generation Resource and
completed the requirements in Section 5.3.2.2, Full Interconnection Study Scoping Process, as a
co-located Large Load, by July I 0, 2026. The FIS must reflect the full requested Load amount and
conform to all study requirements detailed in Section 5.3.2.2.
Option 4 (Studied Load - Dual FIS+ ILLE Pathway): The Large Load has requested an Initial
Energization date on or after January 1, 2028, and ERCOT has detennined that the Large Load
was included in an LLIS request submitted to ERCOT and completed the requirements in Section
9.3.2, Large Load Interconnection Study Scoping Process, by July 10, 2026; and ERCOT has
determined that the ILLE is co-located with a Generation Resource under a Full Interconnection
Study for a new large Generation Resource and completed the requirements in Section 5.3.2.2 by
July 10, 2026. The LLIS and the FIS must be co-located at a single POI, POIB, or Service Delivery
Point.
      Options 1 and 3 address the most straightforward BYOG structure, in which the co-located
generator and load are studied together under a single FIS with the load modeled behind-the-meter
at the shared POI. Options 2 and 4 address the more common scenario in which separate FIS and
ILLE applications have been submitted for projects at the same site, ensuring that BYOG projects
already in the load queue are not disqualified solely because they pursued load interconnection
independently of the generation study. Taken together, the four options ensure that no BYOG
project is structurally excluded from Batch Zero based solely on the absence of a standalone
LLIS-while preserving the study integrity requirements that ERCOT and the Commission have
identified as essential to reliable Batch Zero outcomes.

                                        IV.   Conclusion
     Engine No. 1 respectfully urges the Commission to: 1) direct ERCOT and stakeholders to
develop BYOG eligibility criteria for incorporation into the final PGRR 145 for Batch Zero; and,
2) consider the four BYOG options described above as a starting point for that discussion.
      These recommendations support Texas's stated policy goals of attracting large load
investment and ensure that the Batch Zero process operates fairly and predictably for all large load
interconnection applicants-including those pursuing innovative BYOG co-location models that
can simultaneously add generation capacity and serve new load. We look forward to the continued
discussion at ERCOT and at the Commission on this matter.
